newsitem.title: CANADA: Gunfire briefly halts Arakis drilling in Sudan.
newsitem.headline: Gunfire briefly halts Arakis drilling in Sudan.

text.p: Arakis Energy Corp confirmed reports on Monday of a shooting incident overnight at a southern Sudan drilling location.
No injuries or damage were reported.
"There was an incident in the field," Arakis chief executive John McLeod said in an interview. "We shut the rig down for a few hours and we're back drilling again this morning."
McLeod said responsibility for what had been reported as machine gun fire had not yet been claimed.

Arakis late last week said it agreed to a long-awaited joint venture deal to develop its 12.2 million acre oil concession in southern Sudan and build a 950-mile pipeline to the Red Sea. The cost of the development was estimated at about US$1 billion.

The Canadian company has often received threats from Sudanese rebel groups that claim that money raised from oil development would be used by the Khartoum government to step up Sudan's 13-year civil war.
One rebel group, the Sudan People Liberation Army, said in Nairobi that it was not responsible for the most recent attack.
Arakis receives military protection from the Sudanese Army.
McLeod said he had few other details of what he described as an "incident," but said the situation was under control on Monday.
